hypothesis: Where the first-order separation eps j(s) vanishes (conjugate or focal points) the true separation is of higher order in eps, so the relative first-order error diverges there; past the zero the separation changes sign (image inversion); symmetric configurations raise the order of the true separation.
input_data: Torus(2, 1): outer equator start (0, 0) heading 0; generic start (0, 0.3) heading 0.5
eps = [0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04] rad; RK4 grid with node 400 at s*, 580 steps
Unit sphere: start (pi/2, 0) heading 1.0; grid h = pi/256 to 1.5 pi; eps = 0.02
mathematical_model: Unit-speed geodesics with j'' + K j = 0; d(s; eps) = eps j(s) + r(eps, s). At s* with j(s*) = 0, d(s*) = r(eps, s*). Torus(2, 1) outer equator: K = 1/3, s* = pi sqrt(3); a reflection theta -> -theta makes the normal offset odd in eps and the O(eps^2) along-track lag -eps^2 sin(2 w s)/(4 w) vanish at s*, so d(s*) = O(eps^3). Unit sphere: all great circles through a point refocus exactly at s = pi; the combined perturbation (lateral eps, heading eps) has j = eps (cos s + sin s) with zero at 3pi/4 where the exact chord is eps^2/2 + O(eps^3).
numerical_result: Equator: s* = 5.4414, chord(s*) exponent 3; generic: s* = 6.0514, exponent 2.023; divergence slope -0.9912 (generic), -1.012 (equator); relative error 3.796 one step before s* at eps = 0.04; after s* signed/(eps j) = 0.99588 with j < 0; chord(s*)/chord(s*/2) = 0.000157; sphere relative error uniform -1.667e-05 (max deviation 7.7e-08); sphere combined perturbation chord(3pi/4) = 0.5 eps^2.
observation_model: Embedded chord |X_eps(s) - X(s)| and its signed component along the base geodesic's embedded in-surface normal, compared at matched arclength nodes; no renormalization.
